    #96901. Tech stocks see monster rally after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (510 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech stocks see monster rally after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (510 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, sharply reversing Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020.
    • According to recent reports, shares of Nvidia surged 31.48% after the firm confirmed Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.
    • In a recent development, nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, sharply reversing Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020.

    According to recent reports, shares of Nvidia surged 31.48% after the firm confirmed Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. The semiconductor giant gained back nearly $1 trillion in market cap, posting its best day since May 2003.

    In a recent development, nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month. The organization has been embattled as reports surfaced about Huang's multiple extramarital affairs — one of which was with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang resigned as CEO of the company he founded on Nov. 12.

    In a recent development, the Nasdaq Composite surged 6.51% Monday, for its best day since April 9, 2025. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week, with tech stocks having a rocky week as investors remained nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026.

    Shares of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade saw a lift Monday on the Nvidia news.

    It has been revealed that shares of Alphabet surged 6.34%, Meta gained 6.55%, Amazon jumped 3.47% and Microsoft increased 1.65%. SpaceX added 4.35%, Arm Holdings surged 16.08% and AMD added 6.85%. Dell and Micron posted some of the sector's biggest gains of the day, gaining 20.46% and 19.04%, respectively. The iShares Semiconductor ETF gained 13.63%.

    According to recent reports, neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months amid AI boom financing concerns, surged on Huang's reinstatement. Nebius soared 20.28%, CoreWeave gained 22.32% and Iren gained 23.86%.

    Following a brief premarket surge, Anthropic shares posted a decline of 1.43% in its third day of trading. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing down 8.5% on Friday.

    Speaking to CNBC's Eamon Javers about Huang's reinstatement, President Donald Trump on Monday remarked that last week's market sell-off "probably" influenced his support for the ousted CEO's return.

    It has been revealed that "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump mentioned on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street.".

    Trump said he spoke to Nvidia's board directly and that he "convinced" the board to reinstate Huang, who the president said "did nothing wrong.".

    Industry observers note that "That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market with it," Trump remarked, referring to Nvidia's stock price.

    "The board was in a bad position, but they were put in an easier position to do this when the stock lost 50% of its value or whatever the number was," the president mentioned.

    #96893. Latest Update: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a big buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (417 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a big buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (417 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    Industry observers note that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," stated Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, fresh technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    Sources indicate that the Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    According to recent reports, in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the massive losses.

    It has been revealed that the fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she noted. "That's how crazy things were.".

    • Recent findings suggest that trump had already added artificial intelligence czar to Clayton's portfolio in October.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has been tapped to serve as acting national cyber director while the Trump administration's permanent nominee for the role awaits Senate confirmation, a White House official told CNBC on Monday.

    Recent findings suggest that trump had already added artificial intelligence czar to Clayton's portfolio in October. The official asked not to be named because the pick hasn't been revealed.

    The White House last week revealed that President Donald Trump had picked Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to lead the Office of the National Cyber Director.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. cyber director advises the president on cybersecurity and coordinates U.S. cyber policy across federal agencies. Federal law states that a person may not serve as an acting officer if the president has submitted that person's nomination to the Senate for full appointment and if that person served as first assistant to the office for less than 90 days.

    Davies would replace Sean Cairncross, who was confirmed to the role in August 2025 and whose departure was first reported by Axios last week.

    Trump, at a White House press conference on Friday, stated he decided to replace Cairncross "because I didn't think that person was good enough.".

    Breaking: NBA viewership off to record start, national games up 37% from last season

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (320 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • NBA viewership is off to a record start this season.
    • The league announced Monday that viewership over the first month of the 2026-27 campaign is up 20% from last year on nationally broadcast games on NBC, ESPN and Amazon.
    • The numbers are a solid increase for the league as it enters the second year of a latest massive 11-year media rights deal, which will run through the 2035-36 season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NBA viewership is off to a record start this season.

    The league announced Monday that viewership over the first month of the 2026-27 campaign is up 20% from last year on nationally broadcast games on NBC, ESPN and Amazon. National games are averaging a record 2.62 million viewers, too, which is up about 37% from last season.

    The numbers are a solid increase for the league as it enters the second year of a latest massive 11-year media rights deal, which will run through the 2035-36 season. The new deal extended games with ABC and ESPN, brought national games back to NBC and Amazon Prime Video entered the fold, too. Roughly 75 regular-season games are set to be broadcast on national TV each season, up from just the minimum 15 under the previous agreement.

    Sources indicate that the league also revealed that viewership of live games on NBA League Pass and through the NBA app is up 50%. NBA Cup games on Prime Video are breaking records, too. Those tournament games are averaging about 2 million viewers each so far this season, which is up 90% from last season. The NBA Cup is in its fourth season of existence.

    Industry observers note that the viewership spike comes after a massive showing during the NBA Finals last season. The series between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs averaged roughly 20.6 million views on ABC and ESPN, which made it the most-watched NBA Finals in nearly three decades.

    Viewership numbers are calculated through Nielsen, which shifted to a new methodology in recent years that pairs both big data from smart TV and traditional panel boxes.

    While the season still has a long way to go to live up to the NBA Finals numbers that the Knicks and Spurs drew last spring, it's clear that the league's new media deal is off to a very impressive start.

    #96877. Breaking: More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (658 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say.
    • Industry observers note that net investment income tax, or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly.
    • Unlike the federal income tax or capital gains brackets, the NIIT earnings limits don't adjust annually for inflation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say.

    Industry observers note that net investment income tax, or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly. The tax was enacted in 2010 under President Barack Obama to help fund healthcare via the Affordable Care Act.

    Unlike the federal income tax or capital gains brackets, the NIIT earnings limits don't adjust annually for inflation.

    As a result, "more clients get hit every year," stated certified financial planner Michael Walstedt, founding advisor of Reliant Wealth Advisory in Hoboken, Upcoming Jersey.

    Roughly 5.6% of tax returns included NIIT for 2025, according to IRS data released in November for returns processed through mid-July 2026. That's up from about 3.7% for the same time frame in 2021.

    As more investors pay NIIT, here are some key things to know.

    NIIT applies when you have investment income and your earnings exceed the modified adjusted gross income, or MAGI, limits, according to certified financial planner Marianela Collado, CEO of Tobias Financial Advisors in Plantation, Florida.

    "The trick is to keep an eye on both of these numbers," noted Collado, who is also a certified public accountant and member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council.

    For the NIIT earnings limit, MAGI is typically the same as adjusted gross income, or AGI. One exception would be if you have foreign income, which changes the calculation. You can find last year's AGI on line 11a of your 2025 tax return.

    Married filing jointly: $250,000.

    Married filing separately: $125,000.

    Head of household (with qualifying person): $200,000.

    Qualifying widow(er) with dependent child: $250,000.

    In a recent development, NIIT applies to investment income, which includes interest, dividends, annuities, royalties, certain rents, and more. It can also include capital gains from a primary home sale, for profits that exceed the IRS exclusions. The exclusion is $250,000 for single filers or $500,000 for married couples.

    It has been revealed that the levy stacks on top of regular income tax rates, or capital gains tax — which can be 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on earnings. That means higher earners can pay up to 23.8% on investment income, including long-term capital gains and NIIT.

    The NIIT calculation is 3.8% multiplied by the lesser of:.

    For example, if your MAGI is $30,000 above the NIIT earnings limit and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would pay 3.8% of $30,000, or $1,140.

    Alternatively, if your MAGI is $120,000 above the threshold and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would owe 3.8% of $100,000, or $3,800.

    As year-end approaches, investors should run projections to estimate their adjusted gross income, which can impact NIIT, among other tax consequences, experts say.

    If you're above the NIIT limits, you could reduce AGI by boosting pretax 401(k) deferrals or health savings account contributions, according to Collado with Tobias Financial Advisors.

    According to recent reports, while employee 401(k) deferrals must happen by Dec. 31, you have until next year's tax deadline for health savings account contributions for 2026.

    It has been revealed that you might also try to avoid selling assets before year-end, which could further boost AGI, experts say. Of course, any current-year tax moves should consider your long-term financial goals.

    Amid recent stock market volatility, investors may also consider so-called tax-loss harvesting, which uses losses to offset other portfolio gains, Walstedt with Reliant Wealth Advisory stated.

    Sources indicate that if your losses exceed profits, you can subtract up to $3,000 from regular income. After that, you can carry remaining losses into future tax years.

    However, if you're planning to reinvest the sale proceeds, you need to know the "wash sale rule," which blocks the tax-loss harvesting tax break for buying a "substantially identical" asset within 30 days before or after the sale.

    #96873. As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (433 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (433 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    In a recent development, as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the newly introduced tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders significant and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    #96871. ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (764 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the major averages of U.S.
    • It has been revealed that the relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory.
    • That sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the major averages of U.S. equities surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, giving investors some hope that the relentless selling pressure seen last week may subside — at least temporarily.

    It has been revealed that the relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory. The S&P alone tumbled more than 9% after Huang's departure from the chipmaker was initially announced on Nov. 12 through Friday.

    That sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts. But key questions linger around Nvidia and the artificial intelligence trade that has carried the bull market.

    "I think the AI trade is back on," remarked Mark Gibbens, founder of Gibbens Capital Management. "I certainly believe this establishes a bottom and a floor in the AI trade and the recent market weakness.".

    He added that the news likely doesn't alleviate all concerns that have driven recent declines, including worries about data center approvals after the midterms and fears that the capital expenditures cycle may have peaked. But Gibbens thinks the "keystone" role that Nvidia plays in both financing the AI buildout and the technology's supply chain means a more stable picture of the chipmaker creates a brighter view of the overall market than before.

    In a recent development, an encouraging sign that the correction may be over came even before Nvidia's Monday announcement, according to Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management. He said Friday's selling, which was indiscriminate and affected sectors beyond just AI-exposed companies, indicated a bottom may have been building.

    "Sometimes you just hit that crescendo where you know the market gets oversold, and I would argue that we'd be higher today, even without the Nvidia news," he stated. Indeed, futures tied to the major stock indexes were broadly higher on Sunday night, before any news regarding Huang's return. "So I think that sort of signals we've likely found a place where we priced in, at least the near term, as much of the bad news that was giving markets jitters over the course of the last several weeks.".

    Strengthening the case for a bottom was that the technology sector's forward earnings valuation was cheaper than that of consumer staples, Hogan said. The S&P 500 consumer staples sector trades at a 20.5 multiple, per FactSet. Tech, meanwhile, trades at 16.3 times forward earnings. Hogan said that discrepancy doesn't square with the earnings outlook for the former sector.

    Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, said Huang's return created a relief rally for a market that was oversold. But he's not sure the headline alone can get the market out of its funk.

    "I think the rally will probably fizzle out because now people will pull back and still have the same questions we had before he was replaced," Woods stated. Those questions will likely play out in congressional hearings, he speculated. "The market needed this jolt to get us back on our feet, but it is still a counter trend rally in an otherwise near-term downtrend.".

    Woods, though, stated that the lows for the year are likely in, thanks to Friday's wash-out that spread to all sectors beyond those dependent on Nvidia's role in AI.

    It has been revealed that while investors celebrated Huang's return, the sell-off that accelerated after his departure started before worries about his position even began. That stemmed from concerns about financing the buildout, data center approvals after Democratic wins in the midterm elections and worries that hyperscaler capex may have already peaked or is about to.

    That's why Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, is still nervous about the "picks and shovels" companies involved in the AI trade, a group he says includes Nvidia.

    Industry observers note that "We should enjoy this rally, and maybe it lasts a bit, but I think that picks and shovels trade is going to be solely dependent on what that rate of capex spend is going to be," he mentioned. "That, at the end of the day, is the story that those companies are going to have to deal with outside of bounces like we're seeing now.".

    Traders at Goldman Sachs put it more succinctly.

    "Not sure yet whether good or bad that the fate of the market is almost equal to the fate of one person. But hey ... We are not picky here," they stated.

    — CNBC's Michelle Fox and Deena Zaidi contributed reporting.

    #96865. Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 31%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1029 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 31%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1029 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.
    • The board of directors noted it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.
    • President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.

    The board of directors noted it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".

    Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The Newly introduced York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.

    It has been revealed that shares of Nvidia closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6.

    It has been revealed that "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.".

    Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That upgrade prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people noted.

    Huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations.

    According to recent reports, trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump noted the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Firm, but the American Economy.".

    Sources indicate that he reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote.

    Industry observers note that several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected.".

    Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    Recent findings suggest that for weeks following Huang's ouster, the company's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

    It has been revealed that nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether manufacturer secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it.".

    In a recent development, "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Firm.".

    Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China.

    Lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement Monday.

    Recent findings suggest that huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his plans to testify.

    Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., remarked Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls.".

    Industry observers note that "Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday.

    WATCH: The rise, reinvention and uncertain future of Nvidia without Jensen Huang.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that nvidia's board has officially reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, igniting a roughly 28% relief rally into the low-$160s after last week's brutal sell-off drove shares down to $125.53. While Huang's return removes a major leadership vacuum, the stock still sits far below its $243.37 52-week high and autumn trading ranges above $200.

    It has been revealed that trapped shareholders now face a classic post-crash hurdle: heavy overhead supply. Investors who bought near prior peaks often use sharp rebounds to exit at breakeven, creating stubborn technical resistance between $175 and $210 — especially with congressional testimony and export scrutiny still lingering.

    Rather than waiting passively for a full V-shaped surge to all-time highs, underwater holders can deploy a stock repair strategy geared toward a partial recovery.

    For every 100 shares of NVDA held, an investor can overlay a January 17/195 1x2 call ratio spread for a net debit of $1.10 ($110 per lot):.

    Recent findings suggest that because elevated post-event implied volatility inflates the value of the two short $190 calls, traders can finance nearly the entire cost of the long $170 call for just $1.10 out of pocket. This structure acts as a leveraged recovery accelerator across the 175-to-195 resistance zone without adding margin risk, since one short call is covered by the existing shares and the other by the long $175 call. At January expiration, three outcomes govern the position:.

    The trade-off is capped upside above $214.90, making the strategy ideal for shareholders who view 195–215 as a realistic medium-term ceiling rather than a mere pit stop.

    #96854. CrowdStrike CEO defends Zscaler acquisition, calls it a 'winning combination'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (694 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    CrowdStrike CEO defends Zscaler acquisition, calls it a 'winning combination'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Monday defended the cybersecurity tech giant's planned acquisition of Zscaler, arguing the deal will strengthen its security capabilities and create significant growth opportunities despite a sharp sell-off in its shares.
    • "When you look at the tailwinds from these agentic attacks and you listen to customers, they're looking for a complete solution and a platform that delivers not only all of the capabilities we have, but also has network visibility, protection, and control, and zero trust from a network perspective," Kurtz told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." "This is why we acquired Zscaler today.
    • Shares of CrowdStrike fell roughly 9% Monday after the manufacturer revealed it would acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $44 billion, raising investor concerns about dilution.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Monday defended the cybersecurity tech giant's planned acquisition of Zscaler, arguing the deal will strengthen its security capabilities and create significant growth opportunities despite a sharp sell-off in its shares.

    "When you look at the tailwinds from these agentic attacks and you listen to customers, they're looking for a complete solution and a platform that delivers not only all of the capabilities we have, but also has network visibility, protection, and control, and zero trust from a network perspective," Kurtz told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." "This is why we acquired Zscaler today. The technology, the team, and we think it's a winning combination putting it together with the CrowdStrike platform.".

    Shares of CrowdStrike fell roughly 9% Monday after the manufacturer revealed it would acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $44 billion, raising investor concerns about dilution. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Zscaler shares rose more than 17%.

    The acquisition overshadowed CrowdStrike's better-than-expected quarterly results released Monday morning. The manufacturer had been scheduled to report earnings on Dec. 1, but moved up the release date to coincide with the Zscaler announcement.

    The acquisition fills a key gap in CrowdStrike's cybersecurity platform. While its Falcon platform protects devices and cloud systems, Zscaler adds security across the networks connecting them. Kurtz mentioned the deal expands CrowdStrike's addressable market by roughly $185 billion.

    Sources indicate that crowdStrike's largest acquisition to date comes amid a wave of consolidation in the cybersecurity industry as companies ramp up defenses against increasingly sophisticated AI-powered attacks. Recent high-profile hacks and technology outages have heightened concerns about vulnerabilities in corporate systems. CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares having soared about 96% this year entering Monday's session. For its part, Zscaler's stock ended last week down 13% year to date. As of Friday's close, the companies had a combined market value of more than $265 billion, trailing industry leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.

    In a recent development, kurtz also highlighted the potential to sell more products across the combined customer base. He said the companies share only about 2,000 accounts, leaving roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers that do not at the moment use CrowdStrike.

    The companies are "very complementary overall," Kurtz said. "There's very little overlap.".

    He emphasized that the announcement generated an overwhelmingly positive response from customers.

    "Most important, customers demanded it. They loved it, and I can tell you, my phone blew up after the acquisition," Kurtz remarked. "There's so many customers that love both us and Zscaler, and they're excited to see the acquisition news today.".

    To be sure, the all-stock deal has raised concerns about dilution, since CrowdStrike will glitch latest shares to pay for the acquisition, reducing existing shareholders' ownership stakes.

    Kurtz pushed back on those concerns, arguing that the combination will deliver immediate financial benefits. "On a free cash flow per share basis, it's immediately accretive right after close," he said. "With just modest synergies, you're going to have revenue, operating margin, and free cash flow margin accretion.".

    He also downplayed integration risks, pointing to the companies' longstanding technology partnership. That relationship dates back to at least 2019, and the firms declared an expanded partnership in August 2025. "Zscaler is our No. 1 technology partner," Kurtz noted.

    In a separate "Mad Money" interview, Zscaler CEO and Founder Jay Chaudhry emphasized that combining the companies' platforms will better position them to combat a upcoming generation of AI-powered cyberattacks.

    "I think there's some areas where, by bringing the platforms together, we can become the best protection against AI attacks. That's why the timing became vital, and we're coming from strength, both of us," Chaudhry stated.

    #96851. Industry News: Jim Cramer sees more upside for Nvidia stock with Jensen Huang back as CEO

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (548 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Jim Cramer sees more upside for Nvidia stock with Jensen Huang back as CEO

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO, CNBC's Jim Cramer stated Monday.
    • "It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the "Mad Money" host said.
    • According to recent reports, nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO, CNBC's Jim Cramer stated Monday.

    "It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the "Mad Money" host said. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now.".

    According to recent reports, nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure.

    "Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one manufacturer," he noted. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary.".

    Industry observers note that cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership.

    In a recent development, "If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer said.

    Still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates.

    Those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The Fresh York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the manufacturer's growth outlook intact, he said the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock presently trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet.

    "There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer stated.

    "These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer said. "That's my target.".

    • Nvidia closed near $165."People are mostly just trying to collect a lot of premiums through short vol trades and rolls once they heard about Jensen Huang, take advantage of the vol drop more than anything else," Jason DeLorenzo, founder of Volland, an options-analytics software, said by phone.

    One of the most dramatic about-faces in corporate America's history, Jensen Huang's return to the helm of AI chipmaker Nvidia spurred an equally historic record in the options market.More than 11 million options contracts traded on Nvidia stock Monday, the most active single day of trading for the stock's options in history. That outpaces the 9 million options traded on the Invesco QQQ Trust, and compares to 14 million traded on the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY).Despite Nvidia's monstrous 31% rally and options volume that was more than five times the 30-day average, positioning in the flows was not abnormally bullish. Of the top 10 trades by dollar amount, two massive put sales stood out, but there were no likely outright call buys, based on data from Barchart and SpotGamma. If there was speculative call-buying, it was dwarfed by big trades between the 160 and 170 strikes, where four million options traded for almost $2 billion.

    Nvidia closed near $165."People are mostly just trying to collect a lot of premiums through short vol trades and rolls once they heard about Jensen Huang, take advantage of the vol drop more than anything else," Jason DeLorenzo, founder of Volland, an options-analytics software, said by phone. "It seems like options traders were all repricing, which created record volume, but did not create any obvious one-sidedness."Just under 6.7 million calls traded versus 4.3 million puts, according to Cboe LiveVol data. About 2.4 million calls were likely initiated by buyers, compared with 1.6 million purchasing puts, exchange data show.Open interest in calls was highest at the 170-strike, while open interest in puts was highest at the 150-strike, Barchart data show.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • In a recent development, on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    In a recent development, on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    Recent findings suggest that on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note noted.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    It has been revealed that in that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    #96831. Fed's John Williams indicates higher interest rates likely 'over time' to address inflation

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (423 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Fed's John Williams indicates higher interest rates likely 'over time' to address inflation

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • New York Federal Reserve President John Williams noted Monday that policymakers have more work to do to bring inflation under control, though he indicated that further action can unfold over time as the economy continues to grow.
    • Recent findings suggest that in remarks consistent with previous statements, the influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 before hitting the goal the following year.
    • "But getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential," he noted in remarks at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    New York Federal Reserve President John Williams noted Monday that policymakers have more work to do to bring inflation under control, though he indicated that further action can unfold over time as the economy continues to grow.

    Recent findings suggest that in remarks consistent with previous statements, the influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 before hitting the goal the following year. He also remarked that while artificial intelligence is pressuring prices, there's "little evidence" it will be the source of more persistent inflation.

    "But getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential," he noted in remarks at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York. "We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis. There is still work to do to get that done.".

    The comments come at a delicate moment for monetary policy, as the economy continues to grow and inflation stays well above the Fed's goal.

    Fed officials have differed over how rapidly to raise rates, with some advocating more aggressive action while others, including Williams, have emphasized a measured approach.

    It has been revealed that williams ascribed the current inflation pressures to the conflict in Iran, demand for goods associated with the AI build-out and tariffs, the effects of which he said "have largely abated" as a source of pressure. Nevertheless, he expressed confidence that inflation will subside substantially in 2027 even as economic growth remains robust and unemployment edges lower.

    The Federal Open Market Committee next meets on Dec. 8-9, with markets fully pricing in a quarter percentage point interest rate increase from the current target range of 3.75%-4%. The remarks from Williams are expected to be the last major policy statement from any Fed official before the December decision.

    "Monetary policy cannot move ships or reopen pipelines and refineries, but it can — and must — ensure that these shocks do not lead to broader or persistent inflationary dynamics or erode well-anchored inflation expectations," Williams mentioned, according to his prepared remarks.

    Williams did not explicitly address the December meeting expectations, instead pointing to the statement released after the prior FOMC meeting in late October that noted the "accumulation of more information" will help decide the future policy path.

    "The data that we have received since then show that the economy has remained strong and that inflation has continued to run too high," he mentioned.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Aviation Administration noted Monday it will investigate a recent Amazon drone crash near Detroit.

    On Friday, one of Amazon's MK30 drones "landed on a resident's garage" during a delivery in Huntington Woods, Michigan, a suburb north of Detroit, Amazon spokesperson Jack Stelzner told CNBC in a statement.

    According to recent reports, the crash occurred after the drone dropped off a customer's shampoo order around 4:30 p.m. local time, and one of its propellers was damaged in the incident, according to ABC affiliate WXYZ.

    A preliminary incident report posted to the FAA's website states the drone "struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff." The report claims the condition of the drone is unknown.

    Stelzner mentioned there were no injuries, the drone has been removed and Amazon is in contact with the resident.

    "Safety is our top priority and incidents are extremely rare," Stelzner noted. "Anytime a delivery does not go as planned we investigate what happened and use the findings to further improve the service.".

    It has been revealed that an FAA spokesperson confirmed it's investigating the incident. A spokesperson for the National Transportation Safety Board, a federal agency that also investigates aviation accidents, mentioned it's aware of the incident and is continuing to gather information. The agency hasn't yet determined whether it will open a probe, the NTSB spokesperson added.

    Sources indicate that amazon has been working to make widespread drone delivery a reality ever since founder Jeff Bezos laid out his vision for the program nearly 13 years ago. The rollout has been slow, as the program encountered regulatory delays and staff cuts, as well as technical challenges and pushback from some communities where it conducted early pilots.

    Expansion has recently ramped up. The firm is targeting a launch of its drone service in 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of the year, while an Amazon executive claimed it has the "highest demand drone delivery service in the industry," CNBC previously reported.

    Sources indicate that the e-commerce giant has encountered some challenges along the way. Federal investigators opened a probe nearly one year ago after an Amazon drone downed an internet cable in Waco, Texas. One month earlier, a separate federal probe was opened into an incident near Phoenix, where two Amazon drones collided with a construction crane.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The final week of NBA Cup group play is here, with games on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. Only five teams have been eliminated so far, with 25 teams still battling for the eight spots in the knockout stage, which will take place Dec. 4-11.

    Who will advance? Here's a look at the current standings, remaining schedule and stakes in each group.

    Note: Ties will be broken by (in sequential order): head-to-head record in group play; point differential; total points scored; 2025-26 regular-season record; and, if necessary, a random drawing.

    Magic, Raptors, Pistons can still win group.

    Clinching scenarios for Tuesday and Wednesday.

    Magic clinch group with a win, and clinch home-court advantage in quarterfinals with a win + Celtics or Heat loss.

    Pistons eliminated with: a loss + Wizards win; or a loss + Bucks win; or a loss + Heat and Cavs wins.

    Nets eliminated with: a Wizards win; or a Nets loss, or Heat and Cavs wins.

    Remaining schedule (all times ET).

    Tuesday: Detroit at Orlando, 7 p.m.

    Wednesday: Brooklyn at Milwaukee, 8 p.m.

    Friday: Milwaukee at Detroit, 7:30 p.m.

    Friday: Brooklyn at Toronto, 7:30 p.m.

    Heat, Cavs, 76ers, Pacers, Knicks are all still alive.

    Clinching scenarios for Tuesday and Wednesday.

    Cavs eliminated with loss + Wizards and Heat wins; or various point-differential scenarios.

    76ers eliminated with loss + Wizards or Cavs win.

    Pacers eliminated with Wizards and Heat wins; or Wizards and Cavs wins; or Heat and Cavs wins.

    Knicks eliminated with a loss or Wizards and Heat wins.

    Remaining schedule (all times ET).

    Sources indicate that wednesday: Miami at Philadelphia, 5 p.m. (ESPN).

    Wednesday: Cleveland at Fresh York, 7:30 p.m.

    Friday: Miami at New York, 7 p.m. (Prime).

    Friday: Philadelphia at Indiana, 7:30 p.m.

    Celtics, Hawks, Wizards can still win group.

    Clinching scenarios for Tuesday and Wednesday.

    Wizards eliminated with: a loss + Hornets win; or a loss + Bulls tiebreaker win; or a loss + Heat and Cavs wins or Knicks win by seven or fewer points; or a loss by 18 or more points + Pistons and Nets wins.

    Bulls eliminated with: a loss; or a Wizards win; or tiebreaker loss to Wizards; or Heat and Cavs wins; or Pistons and Nets wins + a win by 13 or fewer points.

    Remaining schedule (all times ET).

    Industry observers note that tuesday: Boston at Washington, 8 p.m. (NBC).

    Wednesday: Chicago at Charlotte, 7 p.m.

    Friday: Atlanta at Boston, 8 p.m.

    Mavericks, Nuggets, Suns can still win group.

    Rockets can only earn wild card.

    Clinching scenarios for Tuesday and Wednesday.

    Mavericks clinch group with a win and Suns loss.

    Nuggets clinch group with a win.

    Suns are eliminated with: a loss + Mavs win; or a loss + Thunder and Grizzlies wins; or a loss + Warriors and Blazers wins.

    Rockets are eliminated with: a loss; or a Mavs win; or a win by four or fewer points; or Thunder and Grizzlies wins; or Warriors and Blazers wins.

    Remaining schedule (all times ET).

    Wednesday: Phoenix at Houston, 8:30 p.m.

    Friday: Dallas at Phoenix, 9 p.m.

    Friday: Denver at Utah, 9:30 p.m.

    Clinching scenarios for Tuesday and Wednesday.

    Timberwolves clinch group with a win + Grizzlies loss.

    Thunder clinch group with a win + Clippers loss.

    Thunder are eliminated with: a loss + Clippers win; or a loss + Nuggets and Suns wins; or a loss + Warriors and Blazers wins.

    Grizzlies are eliminated with: a loss + Wolves win; or a loss + Nuggets and Suns wins; or a loss + Warriors and Blazers wins.

    Clippers are eliminated with: a loss + Thunder win; or a loss + Nuggets and Suns wins; or a loss + Warriors and Blazers wins.

    Remaining schedule (all times ET).

    Wednesday: Minnesota at Oklahoma City, 7:30 p.m. (ESPN).

    Friday: Memphis at Minnesota, 8:30 p.m.

    Friday: New Orleans at LA Clippers, 9:30 p.m.

    Spurs, Lakers, Blazers, Warriors still alive.

    Clinching scenarios for Tuesday and Wednesday.

    Blazers are eliminated with: a loss + Kings win; or a loss + Nuggets and Suns wins; or a loss + Thunder and Grizzlies wins.

    Warriors are eliminated with: a loss + Nuggets and Suns wins; or a loss + Thunder and Grizzlies wins.

    Remaining schedule (all times ET).

    In a recent development, wednesday: San Antonio at Portland, 10 p.m. (ESPN).

    Wednesday: Sacramento at Golden State, 10 p.m.

    Friday: LA Lakers at San Antonio, 9:30 p.m. (Prime).

    Friday: Golden State at Portland, 9:30 p.m.

    Recent findings suggest that the eight teams that advance from group play will take part in a single-elimination tournament. The NBA Cup quarterfinals will be held on Dec. 4 and 5, with the semifinals on Dec. 8 and/or 9, with the higher-seeded teams hosting matchups in their home arenas. The top two teams will advance to the NBA Cup Final on Dec. 11.

    Players of the teams that participate in the knockout stage will earn prize money.

    (During the knockout stage, the 22 teams that didn't qualify will each play two to-be-determined, regular-season games.).

    Recent findings suggest that the NBA Cup is leaving Las Vegas, where the league has held the semifinals and championship game for the past three years. This year, the final will be held at Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.
    • The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the manufacturer's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers said.
    • "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.

    The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the manufacturer's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers said.

    "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a China hawk who is retiring from Congress, told CNBC in a phone interview. "To me it's a failure of character.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC in an extended interview later Monday morning that he personally intervened to convince Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, saying, "I made the deal.".

    Bacon, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation, stated he wants the next Congress to conduct thorough oversight, while questioning the Trump administration's motives.

    In a recent development, "Somebody's responsible for this, and it may be" Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department is responsible for setting U.S. export controls on AI chips, Bacon remarked. "But I think we should get to the bottom of this.".

    Huang, who is scheduled to testify before multiple committees on Capitol Hill starting Dec. 1, is "going to get high scrutiny in a bipartisan way when he comes next week," Bacon said.

    Huang's closed-door appearance before a trio of House committees is on the schedule, as the panels seek answers on the national security implications of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, MS NOW reported. The Senate banking committee declared after Huang's reinstatement that he will appear for a public hearing Dec. 3.

    John Fisher of Trident, a spokesman for Huang, declined to comment on the Nvidia CEO's scheduled appearances.

    "He better be there," Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told CNBC about Huang's scheduled Dec. 1 appearance. His reinstatement will only intensify congressional probes into Nvidia and its government connections, Amo predicted.

    "I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query, and it makes Howard Lutnick and his dealings — supporting his nepo children's operation at Cantor Fitzgerald — party to inquiry as well as any other administration official that has facilitated a status quo in which chips can be sold to China or Chinese operated intermediaries who don't intend good things for the American people," said Amo, referring to the financial firm run by Lutnick's sons that has business ties to Nvidia.

    A Cantor spokesperson didn't comment directly when asked about Amo's comments, saying the firm "holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia" and noting its Nvidia positions "arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients.".

    The Commerce Department didn't immediately respond to requests to comment on Bacon's and Amo's remarks.

    Nvidia in a statement Monday mentioned it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    David Rudenstine, a constitutional law professor and national security scholar at Cardozo School of Law, mentioned the frenzy around Huang's comeback is secondary to lingering national security concerns."The real responsibility for national security is with the administration and not with the CEO of a private tech giant," Rudenstine told CNBC."You're opposed to China getting the chips. You recognize that the intermediary companies are sending chips to China, and you don't put a stop to it. I don't get it," he said.

    The CEO's reinstatement, while celebrated by the White House and in Silicon Valley, led to heightened calls on Capitol Hill to seek answers on AI chip exports to China and what the Trump administration's role has been in facilitating that.

    "We are sending high-end computer chips to China, and yet we're saying we want to win the AI war. It's a contradiction, and it's a failure of leadership in the White House," Bacon told CNBC.

    It has been revealed that sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, told CNBC in an emailed statement that Huang's return "proves that under Trump, Vance, and Rubio, national security is for sale to the highest bidder.".

    Industry observers note that "We will all pay the price of letting China plunder America's cutting edge technology. Democrats will be pushing for accountability for anyone in the administration that put corrupt deals over our country's security," Wyden, who is also a Senate Intelligence Committee member, said.

    It has been revealed that trump in a Truth Social post Monday added that Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Lawmakers, who have already rolled out multiple investigations related to Huang, Nvidia and related entities, quickly filed in to question those conclusions.

    Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., a close Trump ally and a former CEO, criticized the move and called for a congressional briefing "as soon as possible" on Huang's reinstatement.

    "Nvidia's board is free to vote however they want, but the federal government owes the American people answers about what actually happened," Scott told CNBC in an emailed statement. "This looks terrible on its face, and it drives home the need for Congress to be informed on the full impact of Jensen Huang's actions on our national security and economy.".

    Rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, told CNBC that it's still not clear to what degree Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy might have compromised national security.

    Recent findings suggest that "The fact that the president of the United States is involved in putting him back in there, presumably because maybe he has stock or he just cares about the stock market, it's really reached a bizarre place," Peters said. "And obviously that man has not learned anything from the election about what people think of him, or he doesn't care.".

    Monday's move also gave fuel to lawmakers who have already questioned Trump, his administration or Nvidia.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the firm's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., remarked in a statement via the Senate Banking Committee, where she is the top Democrat and is expected to become chair in January.

    Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, more tersely questioned the official assurances that Huang poses no risks to national security.

    "No national security risk? Based on what?" he wrote on X.

    Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., who serves on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, in an X post called Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang "outrageous.".

    "We still don't know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia's own board has completed its investigation," wrote Krishnamoorthi, who is also a member of the House Oversight and Intelligence panels.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan, Garrett Downs and Luke Fountain contributed to this report.

    In a recent development, memphis selected Boozer with the No. 3 pick in June's NBA Draft following a freshman season at Duke that earned him consensus National Player of the Year honors. Boozer has so far delivered on his potential as a standout from a rookie class that's projected as one of the best in NBA history.

    In 16 games, Boozer has averaged 16.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks per game. As with most rookies, Boozer has room to improve his efficiency with a 41.7% field-goal rate and a 32.2% success rate from 3. But his dynamic offensive game as a skilled, floor-stretching power forward has translated to the NBA early in his career.

    According to recent reports, boozer's impact has contributed to winning on the floor for Memphis. A Grizzlies team that finished 25-57 last season is off to a 12-5 start, which was good for fifth place in the West going into Monday's games. Boozer has emerged a a leader on the team alongside breakout guard Ty Jerome (24.8 ppg, 5.3 apg) as the Grizzlies look like contenders to return to the postseason.

    They'll look to stay afloat in the top half of the Western Conference standings over the next four weeks without their standout rookie.

    CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: AI race spreads from robots to smartphones

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (914 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing.
    • I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies.
    • It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses.

    I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies. Beneath the fanfare, what's changed on the tech front in what's often dubbed China's Silicon Valley?

    It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.

    Even after a human knocked a box and toys away from their original spots, a LimX robot quickly located them and moved them to pre-set locations. While still far from perfect, the smoothness of the demo contrasted with the robot's more stilted movements I'd seen early this summer — and inability then to react to rapid changes in tasks.

    Sources indicate that when we caught up in Shenzhen last week, CFO Jesse Liu declined to comment on LimX's IPO prepares. But he told me that his conversations around the APEC CEO Summit revealed an excitement around a latest development for humanoids: growing demand for robot chips that can run smarter large language models locally, instead of on the cloud.

    "A lot of chipmakers are now happy about the latest developments in LLMs because they think robotic OEMs will actually begin to integrate more storage, and reasoning, and compute, and inference infrastructure on the edge, or locally inside the robot body," Liu said, referring to original equipment manufacturers.

    "They do see robots moving from hundreds of units to thousands of units, to tens of thousands of units, beginning to enter that kind of automotive quantity," he said, pointing to chip suppliers such as Horizon Robotics.

    Latest AI models, particularly GPT-6 Astra, have shown not just improved reasoning, but better control of robots.

    That puts more of the onus on hardware makers, for robots or other devices, to create practical applications. LimX said it's working with business partners in over 30 markets, including Switzerland where the robots serve as power plant inspectors in rural areas.

    Industry observers note that the key for powering AI's transition into the physical world is on-device chips and more powerful batteries. That means Nvidia's most expensive, cutting-edge chips won't be the only ones powering generative AI models.

    So far, even in basic consumer applications such as smartphones, AI isn't transformative enough to be a top-three selling point for mass-market users, Thomas Bai, AI product expert at smartphone tech giant Honor, told me in Shenzhen.

    He expects that in the next few years, as smartphone chips are able to run more powerful AI models, the "super agent" tech can become better at completing tasks on its own, and anticipating a user's needs — such as ordering coffee.

    Counterpoint on Nov. 19 forecast that in the retail industry, "edge AI" revenue will surge sixfold by 2032, with roughly half of revenue coming from retail robots that clean and check inventory — often with the help of smaller AI models that can run on locally embedded chips.

    But more capable, on-device AI also requires more battery power, Honor's Bai pointed out.

    It has been revealed that honor's X70 Android smartphone, which rolled out last summer, boasts a battery with 8,300 milliampere-hours for a total device weight of just under 200 grams. That compares with 5,000 mAH for the 214-gram flagship Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and roughly 5,400 mAH for this year's 249-gram Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max, according to GSM Arena.

    LimX's Oli humanoid comes with 9,500 mAH battery capacity, lasting the robot about 1.5 hours.

    Such AI applications, however, remain sensitive to the memory-chip shortage weighing on the industry.

    The X70 was the best-selling Android phone in the entry to mid-tier range, said Shenzhen-based Counterpoint analyst Shiwen Ma.

    While Ma said penetration of smartphones with generative AI features is higher in China at 55% versus 38% overseas, the offerings are still not essential to customers, while rising memory-chip costs make it harder for manufacturers to bring AI-powered devices to the mass market.

    Geely-backed automotive tech organization EcarX's CFO Dylan Jeng told me earlier this month he expects the memory price surge to persist through 2027, and even the first half of 2028.

    The chipmaker that can narrow the gap for on-device AI needs could find its moment soon.

    Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged.

    U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke exclusively on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." President Donald Trump on Friday said he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week.

    How China is using summits to expand its global influence.

    For a second year in a row, Xi has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores. But U.S.-China trade, Taiwan and tech tensions remain unresolved as Trump returned from Asia.

    Putin scores 'massive win' at first trilateral meeting.

    It has been revealed that the first-ever three-way summit is "arguably a diplomatic victory for Moscow," noted Andrius Tursa, an advisor for Central and Eastern Europe and Russia at Teneo. The view from inside the APEC welcome banquet indicated the leaders were in close proximity from the start of the summit.
